title: If the maximal ideal is not an associated prime of a finite module, it contains a nonzerodivisor on it
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of $M$, i.e. there is no $z\in M$ with $\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak m$. Then there is an $x\in\mathfrak m$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $x$ on $M$ is injective).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor, line 15471), implication (2) => (1) for $I=\mathfrak m$ (for $I=\mathfrak m$ the condition $\mathfrak m\not\subset\mathfrak q$ for all $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ says $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}(M)$, as $\mathfrak m$ is maximal)
